title: Unit – 1 : Session – 5 : SLO – 1  |  Exokernel and Layered Operating Systems — Word Reassembly
sections: EXOKERNEL — a minimalist kernel that exposes hardware directly to applications through library
operating systems; applications control resource management themselves.
LAYERED STRUCTURE — the OS is divided into layers; each layer uses services only of the layer below
it (layer 0 = hardware, top layer = user interface).
IPC (Inter-Process Communication) — minimal service kept inside small kernels.
LIBRARY OS — in exokernels, untrusted application libraries implement abstractions like files.
MODULARITY — layered design allows debugging and verification layer by layer.
Exokernel: purpose is maximum flexibility and performance by multiplexing hardware securely and
letting applications manage resources via library OSes (e.g. MIT's Aegis/XN).
Layered OS: architecture where functions are grouped into ordered layers; advantage is simplicity
of construction/debugging; disadvantage is overhead of crossing layers and careful layer definition.
